sources: Practices drawn from the CISA #StopRansomware Guide and NIST IR 8374, Ransomware Risk Management: A Cybersecurity Framework Profile. Control references are NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5.

system_checks.title: No backup
system_checks.remediation: Start backing up this system now, with at least one copy kept offline or immutable.

system_checks.title: No offline or immutable backup copy
system_checks.remediation: Keep at least one backup copy that ransomware cannot reach: offline media, an immutable cloud bucket, or a backup service with object lock.

system_checks.title: Backups run less often than the data you can afford to lose
system_checks.remediation: Increase backup frequency, or use snapshots or replication, so the backup interval is within the recovery point objective.

system_checks.title: Recovery would take longer than the business can be down
system_checks.remediation: Shorten recovery: restore from local snapshots, pre-build replacement servers, document the restore steps, or agree a realistic downtime target with the business.

system_checks.title: Restore not tested in the last 12 months
system_checks.remediation: Restore this system to a test environment, confirm the data is usable, and record how long it took.

system_checks.title: Recovery time is an estimate, not measured
system_checks.remediation: Time a real restore so the recovery plan is based on evidence rather than a guess.

system_checks.title: Backups use the same credentials as production
system_checks.remediation: Give the backup system its own accounts, not joined to the production domain, protected with MFA.

system_checks.title: Backup jobs are not monitored for failures
system_checks.remediation: Turn on backup failure alerts and have someone review them daily.

system_checks.title: Backups are not encrypted
system_checks.remediation: Encrypt backups so a stolen copy cannot be read or used for extortion.

practices.label: Incident response plan with a ransomware playbook
Offline or printed copy of the response plan and key contacts
MFA on remote access and email
MFA and separate accounts for backup administration
Endpoint protection on all computers and servers
Internet-facing systems (VPN, firewall, remote access) patched promptly
Email filtering and phishing awareness training
Network segmentation separating backups and critical systems
Administrator accounts separate from everyday accounts
Ransomware tabletop exercise in the last 12 months
